Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

effect noun

what one thing does to another

also have an effect on, have no effect, impact

classical

Cic. Div. 1.73: quod ostentum habuit hanc vim, ut (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Div. 2.47: vim et effectum

vīs, vīs f.

noun, third declension, irregular: accusative vim, ablative vī; plural vīrēs, strength · Declension on Wiktionary

power, force; the effect of a thing

Latin speaks of the power a thing has: vim habēre, to have an effect; the effect of a medicine or a herb is its vīs. What a thing does to someone is often a verb: afficere, movēre.

Other words

  • effectus, effectūs m. — effect, working

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 2.3: effectus ēloquentiae est audientium approbātiō (Lewis & Short); Cic. Div. 2.47: vim et effectum · Declension on Wiktionary

    In Cicero mostly the carrying out of something; of the effect it has, beside vīs.

  • afficiō, afficere, affēcī, affectum — affect, have an effect on (someone)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 5.20.6: nūllā umquam voluptāte tantā sum adfectus · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    With the ablative of what one is made to feel: aliquem laetitiā, dolōre afficere.

  • moveō, movēre, mōvī, mōtum — move, make an impression on

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Phaedr. 3.6.4: verbīs nōn moveor tuīs · Conjugation on Wiktionary

Examples

  • genera herbārum … quārum causam ignōrārēs, vim et effectum vidērēs

    kinds of herbs … whose cause you did not know, but whose power and effect you could seeCic. Div. 2.47

  • cōnsuētūdō enim labōrum perpessiōnem dolōrum efficit faciliōrem

    for being used to hard work makes pain easier to bearCic. Tusc. 2.35

  • respondit illa: verbīs nōn moveor tuīs

    she answered: your words have no effect on mePhaedr. 3.6.4

See also result, cause, strength, affect.
